XRP Ledger Launches Six-Amendment Vote, Unveils Major v3.3.0 Upgrade With Confidential Transfers and Institutional Tools
data.description:
The proposals include Confidential Transfer, Batch, Permission Delegation, Sponsor, Dynamic MPT, and a bundled cleanup amendment. None of these features should be considered active on the XRP Ledger yet. Under the network's amendment process, a proposal must maintain more than 80% validator support for two consecutive weeks before it can activate.

The release follows several months of development work around the next generation of XRP Ledger functionality. Development activity shows support being added across the XRPL software ecosystem for features including Batch V1.1, Dynamic MPT, and the new cleanup amendment ahead of the 3.3.0 release.

XRPL validator Vet described the package as a major release, highlighting privacy, transaction batching, sponsored fees, delegated permissions, and token flexibility among the changes heading into the voting process.

Privacy and transaction upgrades lead the proposal

Confidential Transfer is the most notable privacy-focused proposal in the XRP Ledger v3.3.0 package. According to the official XRPL amendment documentation, the feature is designed to provide institutional-grade privacy for Multi-Purpose Tokens (MPTs) using EC-ElGamal encryption and zero-knowledge proofs.

XRP Ledger v3.3.0 has launched with six proposed amendments now open for validator voting. Source: XRP Ledger Operations via X

The proposed system would shield individual MPT balances and transfer amounts from public view while retaining mechanisms that allow authorized parties, such as issuers or auditors, to verify relevant information. This distinction is important for institutional use cases, where transaction confidentiality may need to coexist with reporting and regulatory requirements.

The Batch amendment addresses a different limitation by allowing multiple transactions to be executed as a single atomic operation. The updated Batch V1.1 implementation has also been incorporated into XRPL developer tooling, including xrpl4j, as work progressed toward the 3.3.0 release.

Atomic execution means the transactions in a batch are treated as one coordinated operation rather than a series of independent actions. That can be useful for more complex settlement flows, including transactions that need several steps to succeed together.

Permission Delegation is aimed at account management and institutional security. The feature allows an account owner to assign specific transaction permissions to another account without handing over control of the primary account's keys.

The approach can separate operational duties from asset custody. For example, an organization could maintain assets in a more secure account while allowing another wallet to perform narrowly defined transactions. The proposal is also a revised version of an earlier Permission Delegation implementation. XRPL developers previously disabled that version after a vulnerability was identified, with PermissionDelegationV1_1 developed as its replacement.

Sponsor introduces another change that could affect how applications interact with the XRP Ledger. It allows one account to cover transaction fees and reserve requirements for another account under defined conditions.

For developers, sponsored costs could make applications easier to use because newcomers would not necessarily need to manage XRP for every initial network interaction. The underlying goal is to reduce friction around account funding and transaction execution.

@Vet_X0, an XRP Ledger validator, calls XRPL v3.3.0 a major release featuring the network’s first native privacy amendment for encrypted MPT balances and transfers. Source: @Vet_X0 via X

Dynamic MPT, meanwhile, focuses on token issuers. The amendment is associated with XLS-94 and is designed to make selected properties of Multi-Purpose Tokens changeable after issuance. That gives issuers additional flexibility when managing tokenized assets whose operational requirements can evolve over time. XRPL documentation currently lists DynamicMPT as an amendment in development.

The sixth proposal, FixCleanup, groups technical fixes intended to improve protocol stability and address issues within the XRP Ledger's implementation.

Together, the amendments cover several different layers of the network. Confidential Transfer focuses on privacy, Batch on transaction composition, Permission Delegation on account control, Sponsor on user experience, and Dynamic MPT on token management.

Performance improvements now await validator approval

The 3.3.0 release also includes infrastructure work intended to improve the experience of running XRP Ledger nodes. Development updates have highlighted efforts to reduce resource requirements and improve synchronization for node operators.

XRPL v3.3.0 introduces Confidential Transfers, using EC-ElGamal encryption and zero-knowledge proofs to shield MPT balances and transfer amounts while preserving cryptographic verifiability. Source: @iamalijandro via X

Earlier reports based on Vet's development updates cited potential memory reductions ranging from roughly 10% to as much as 40% in certain conditions. The more conservative figures associated with the current release indicate memory usage reductions of around 10% to 15%. The exact benefit can vary depending on the node's workload and environment.

Lower resource consumption matters because validators and other node operators must continuously maintain and synchronize ledger data. Improvements in memory efficiency and synchronization can reduce the infrastructure burden associated with operating the network.

The upgrade also reflects the iterative nature of XRP Ledger development. Several components in version 3.3.0 have undergone revisions before reaching the validator stage. Batch and Permission Delegation, in particular, have previously required changes following security reviews and subsequent development work.

The validator vote is therefore the next critical step rather than the final confirmation that the features will become part of the live protocol.

Each amendment must maintain the required supermajority for two consecutive weeks before activation. XRPL's official documentation states that amendments that meet this threshold can become enabled on the mainnet, while proposals that fail to sustain sufficient support do not activate.

If the six proposals clear that process, the XRP Ledger would gain a broader set of native tools for confidential token transfers, atomic transactions, delegated account permissions, sponsored costs, and flexible MPT management.

For institutions exploring tokenized assets, the combination is particularly relevant because it addresses several practical requirements at once: privacy, controlled access, transaction coordination, and token administration. However, the significance of the upgrade will ultimately depend on validator approval and subsequent adoption by developers and network participants.

Zcash: Coinholders vote on NU7 scope - 25 Aug 2026
data.description:
Zcash says coinholders will begin voting on the scope of the upcoming NU7 upgrade on August 25, with the vote expected to last approximately 18 days.

The vote gives holders a direct role in deciding which work is included in the next protocol upgrade. Its relevance comes from the way the outcome can shape Zcash's future technical direction, rather than from an immediate change to the network.

The announcement establishes a governance process, but it does not by itself confirm which proposals will be selected or how the approved scope will be implemented. Those details remain dependent on the vote's result and subsequent upgrade work.

Lithium Price Analysis: Carbonate Holds 142,750 Yuan After Recent Pullback
data.description:
Battery material has seen a modest correction in the past session, adding 1,250yuan or 0.88%, as the overall trend leans toward consolidation after a robust first-half rally. Battery-grade lithium carbonate prices have been volatile as supply and demand fundamentals change across the market.

Lithium Price Finds Support After Lengthy Pullback

The 1-year chart of lithium carbonate illustrates a healthy rebound from late 2025 levels before a correction ensues. Prices increased rapidly in the first few months of 2026 before reaching the levels of almost 200,000 yuan/tonne in May and then easing back to the present 142,750 level.

The diagram shows that LIT is finding a higher band than its 2025 lows. Following the May peak, prices retraced through June and July to create a downward trend. The recent advance towards 142,750yuan reflects the market testing a support zone after falling away from the previous rally.

Today’s daily movement: 0.88% higher as lithium carbonate rebounds from the recent sideways trading sessions. Price has been trading inside a narrow price band near recent lows, indicating lower price volatility relative to the drastic range trading seen earlier in the year.

The short-term structure has resistance building in the 150,000-160,000 yuan area. Above this zone, it would be a greater correction, whereas if it remains weak, it would be targeted towards a lower support area.

Lithium Carbonate Technical Indicators Show Neutral Momentum

Meanwhile, the TradingView chart for other lithium-related assets appears to have a neutral technical setup. The MACD indicator moved to the middle after previous buying momentum weakened. The latest values read MACD 0.01 and histogram -0.08.

This is a sign that the momentum is slowing down after the recent push. The directional indicator is not showing a strong directional movement.

However, the RSI is at about 49.75. The RSI is still at the moderate 50 levels and remains somewhat away from its earlier heavy values, signaling that lithium is no longer witnessing the kind of momentum it had witnessed in the previous rally.

The graph of the lithium stock index displayed another significant intraday move to 242.43. The stock fluctuated primarily between 235 and 238 during the session. The move was enough to take the index away from the recent lows, although momentum indicators showed signs of easing.

Lithium Market Tracks Supply And Demand Shifts

Nonetheless, the lithium carbonate market is still closely following revisions to battery demand, inventory levels, and activity in production. According to market information, lithium prices have recovered from earlier lows and are back up to levels below those seen at the 2026 high earlier this year.

Price evaluations conducted over the past three months highlight the continuing vulnerability of battery-grade lithium carbonate to supply responses to demand from the electric vehicle and energy storage markets.

What is important here, because of the current chart structure, is 142,750 yuan as short-term support. Maintaining this level preserves the recent consolidation scheme; breaking below could carry us down even further.

On the positive side, lithium carbonate has to return to the 150000 yuan level in order to restore a bullish stance in the short term. Overall, the market is still in the consolidation area between the recovery moves and the correction after the May peak.
